purpose: A routable track must declare an address and at least one operation surface, own that address exclusively, and hold the same authority boundary as every other track.

route_surface.rule: an addressable track needs a scheme and at least one operation surface; an address with no operation is a route that cannot be called
route_surface.fallback_note: the router already falls back to capabilities and governs when verbs is empty, so those are declared operations, not implied ones

authority_boundary.rule: one boundary for every track: a track is a routing prior, never a verifier or a committer

ambiguity.scheme_owner: exactly one track per declared scheme
ambiguity.derived_alias: an id-derived alias may be shared, but a declaration settles ownership (see uri-address.contracts.json)
ambiguity.rule: two tracks declaring the same scheme is an ambiguous route surface

coverage_snapshot.note: no track declares URI verbs yet; every track is callable through its capabilities or governs surface

ROUTE1.name: every_track_has_an_address
ROUTE1.check: every shipped track declares at least one scheme

ROUTE2.name: every_address_has_an_operation
ROUTE2.check: every track declares at least one operation surface

ROUTE3.name: addresses_are_exclusive
ROUTE3.check: no two tracks declare the same scheme

ROUTE4.name: the_authority_boundary_is_uniform
ROUTE4.check: no track claims fact, verification or commit authority

ROUTE5.name: the_surface_is_not_sparse
ROUTE5.check: no addressable track has an empty operation surface, and the declared coverage matches the snapshot
